Based on a search of James W. Aageson’s doctoral thesis, Paul's Use of Scripture: A Comparative Study of Biblical Interpretation in Early Palestinian Judaism and the New Testament With Special Reference to Romans 9-11 (Oxford University, 1983), all 12 B001 comparisons are explicitly discussed in the source.
Below is the summary table detailing the page locators (using the original thesis page numbers), depth of discussion, and a concise description for each passage:
B001 ID
	
Discussed
	
Page / Locator
	
Depth
	
Description of Author's Discussion


1. Romans 4:3 / Genesis 15:6
	
YES
	
Pages 69 (fn 19), 70 (fn 69), 138–139, 173, 280
	
Substantive
	
Aageson analyzes how Paul utilizes Genesis 15:6 in Romans 4:3 and Galatians 3:6 (noting word order transposition between ἐπίστευσεν and Ἀβραάμ and the catchword λογίζομαι) to establish his theological distinction between righteousness by faith and circumcision.


2. Romans 9:25 / Hosea 2:23
	
YES
	
Pages 69, 81, 107, 178–179, 215, 273, 281
	
Substantive
	
Aageson examines how Paul substitutes καλέσω for ἐρῶ in Hosea 2:23 (LXX 2:25) to create a deliberate verbal link with Hosea 1:10 (LXX 2:1) and Romans 9:24, substantiating the divine election and calling of the Gentiles.


3. Romans 9:26 / Hosea 1:10
	
YES
	
Pages 69 (fn 19), 107, 178–180, 280
	
Substantive
	
Aageson shows how Paul links Hosea 1:10 (LXX 2:1, following LXX-A) with Hosea 2:23 via the catchword κληθήσονται and with Isaiah 10:22–23 via "sand of the sea" to demonstrate that Gentiles are called sons of the living God.


4. Romans 10:11 / Isaiah 28:16
	
YES
	
Pages 69 (fn 19), 71, 88, 116–117, 180, 182–183, 218, 281
	
Extended
	
Aageson explores Paul's double citation of Isaiah 28:16 in Romans 9:33 and 10:11, explaining that the insertion of πᾶς in 10:11 stems from its association with Joel 2:32 (3:5) to ground universal salvation in Christ.


5. Romans 10:13 / Joel 2:32
	
YES
	
Pages 71 (fn 72), 86, 89, 125–126, 183, 280
	
Substantive
	
Aageson analyzes Paul's use of Joel 2:32 (LXX 3:5) in Romans 10:13, showing how the catchwords πᾶς and ἐπικαλέομαι link it to Isaiah 28:16 and structure Paul's argument that salvation is universally open to Jew and Gentile alike.


6. Romans 11:34 / Isaiah 40:13
	
YES
	
Pages 69 (fn 19), 72, 90, 108, 197, 281
	
Substantive
	
Aageson discusses Paul's double citation of Isaiah 40:13 in Romans 11:34 and 1 Corinthians 2:16, noting that Paul follows LXX-A (σύμβουλος αὐτοῦ) to conclude his doxology on the unsearchable wisdom and judgments of God.


7. Romans 15:12 / Isaiah 11:10
	
YES
	
Pages 90 (fn 16), 107–108, 161 (fn 67), 281
	
Substantive
	
Aageson discusses Paul's citation of Isaiah 11:10 in Romans 15:12, noting how the catchword ἔθνη connects it within a scriptural catena to establish Christ's role in the hope and election of the Gentiles.


8. 1 Corinthians 1:19 / Isaiah 29:14
	
YES
	
Pages 91–92, 108 (fn 53), 281
	
Substantive
	
Aageson examines how Paul cites Isaiah 29:14 in 1 Corinthians 1:19 to establish the scriptural foundation for the "word of the cross" and to develop his thematic exposition on God making foolish the wisdom of the world.


9. 1 Corinthians 6:16 / Genesis 2:24
	
YES
	
Pages 70–71, 104, 150 (fn 50), 280
	
Substantive
	
Aageson analyzes Paul's double citation of Genesis 2:24 in 1 Corinthians 6:16 and Ephesians 5:31, pointing out that Paul adds the syntactical formula γάρ, φησίν in 1 Corinthians to apply the "one flesh" principle ethically to sexual conduct.


10. 1 Corinthians 9:9 / Deuteronomy 25:4
	
YES
	
Pages 68 (fn 15), 81 (fn 63), 93, 107 (fn 55), 113 (fn 119), 149, 280
	
Substantive
	
Aageson discusses Paul's citation of Deuteronomy 25:4 in 1 Corinthians 9:9–10 (noting the lexical variant κημόω for φιμόω) as an explicit exegetical application illustrating the apostle's right to material support.


11. 1 Corinthians 10:7 / Exodus 32:6
	
YES
	
Pages 93 (fn 21), 150, 280
	
Substantive
	
Aageson examines Paul's citation of Exodus 32:6 in 1 Corinthians 10:7 as a midrashic warning drawn from Israel's wilderness experience to exhort the Corinthian church against idolatry.


12. Galatians 3:13 / Deuteronomy 21:23
	
YES
	
Pages 70 (fn 30), 80, 92, 94–95, 102, 113 (fn 118), 160 (fn 19), 280
	
Substantive
	
Aageson addresses Paul's intentional omission of ὑπὸ θεοῦ from Deuteronomy 21:23 in Galatians 3:13, explaining that Paul modified the LXX text for theological reasons to avoid implying that Christ was accursed by God.
